The candidate wheel built with the frame variant carries 52 "singleton
op call with no live install: lower_scope" floors, read out of
.build/m2cache/m2.wat. So lower_state_field_inits runs where lower_scope
is not installed, every ls_* call in the variant lowered to an
unreachable, and the compile trapped: exit 134, zero WAT, backtrace
pinning map$spr_initnNode_nLowExpr under lower_stmt_body — the map the
change itself added.

The site's own comment was right, and this arc spent three iterations
arguing with it. It says the config slot is resolved structurally, the
slot known by name, rather than via a frame the install must thread
evidence for. The frame is unavailable precisely because the install
threads no LowerScope evidence here. The special case is the correct
design given that, not the shortcut I kept calling it.

This also retracts the previous entry's central claim. It reported that
the frame is consulted, on the evidence of zero unbound-name markers in
the variant's WAT. That file was zero bytes: the compile had already
trapped and emitted nothing, so zero matches meant nothing. It is the
same "no verdict from empties" the march's SIZE-GUARD refuses, made by
hand. Check an artifact's byte count before grepping it.

What the real fix must be, now constrained by evidence rather than
taste: the nested case has to be resolved structurally too, config refs
substituted for LUpval(0, slot) within the init's own lowering with no
scope handler involved — a lowering parameterised by config_names, or a
rewrite of the lowered tree. It is the first design in this arc the
artifact has not refused.

Freeverb's eight comb filters each build an IIRFilterNode, and Blink prices
one by simulating its impulse response until it decays: 112 ms per filter on

gives every roll a depth floor, so the boot's own setSend runs inside the
same module evaluation that has to finish before anything paints.

Oscillator.getInitialValue runs a 32-term scan of a 2048-partial inverse
FFT, roughly 131k trig calls, on every LFO construction and every phase
write. Chorus does two at boot and a color swap does four to six more per
dice roll. It is memoized carrying its full side effect, because
_getRealImaginary also rewrites _partialCount and refills _partials with
2047 amplitudes, and both are readable on the instance afterwards.

inactive instead of disposed and rebuilt, which is the same reason the dry
park works. Their LFOs free-run either way, so a reused chain re-enters at a
drifted phase; offline renders build each chain exactly once, so exports
cannot see it.
